data.narrative:
Bright Machines, a Series C robotics and manufacturing automation company that has raised $300M+, is evaluated against a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public company. The peer set includes five primary comparables: Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), Bedrock Robotics (Series B, $1.8B), Dexterity (Series B, $1.6B), Hadrian (Series C, $1.6B), and Nimble Robotics (Series C, $1.0B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $300M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $510M. Peer-median analysis across the five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. The disparity between methods reflects the heterogeneity within early-stage robotics valuations.

Synthesizing both approaches produces a triangulated range of $434M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $1.1B. The stage-progression method anchors to capital deployed, while peer-median reflects current market pricing for comparable robotics firms. Key uncertainties include revenue traction and burn efficiency relative to peers, and whether Bright Machines commands a premium or discount to the Hadrian/Nimble Robotics comparable set at equivalent stage. The wide range reflects genuine valuation dispersion in the sector at this stage.
